- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5–10% overshoot after price surge), apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-stage rallies (last 5–7 days of true outcome); add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 forecast points if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays reaction; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% in first 3–5 days of new sentiment.
